# GOAT Backend Card Logic Implementation Task Queue

## Goal

Codex must complete this dependency-ordered task queue and implement backend game logic for the full GOAT Format card pool represented by `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json`. Foundation, matrix, validation, shared engine, and template work must be established before parallel card work begins. Once those prerequisites are stable, Card Tasks may be executed in parallel shards if each shard owns explicit card-task ranges and all merge and validation gates pass. Testing must use tiered validation: targeted card/template checks at card-task level, shard-local validation before merge, and full repository validation only at shared-surface, shard-merge, and final gates unless the repo test suite is fast enough to run more often.

This task file was generated from the actual `cards.json` source order and contains one explicit Card Task for each source row: **1704 card tasks**.

Progress for this queue is tracked in `docs/implementation-status.md`.

Completion means every card from `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` has verified backend behavior or verified GOAT exclusion. Every GOAT-pool card must end with executable behavior, including forbidden cards that are deck-blocked but still explicitly behavior-covered where applicable.

The final coverage report must show:

```text
goatUnsupported = 0
```

## Operating Rules for Codex

- Respect dependency order rather than blindly serial order.
- Complete repository inspection, frontend/backend contract audit, shared foundation tasks, matrix schema, validators, and the parallel workstream protocol before parallelizing card tasks.
- After prerequisites pass, Card Tasks may be processed in parallel shards by source-index range, Card Task range, template family, risk level, or interaction tags.
- Each card identity must be owned by exactly one shard at a time.
- Each card task must still be individually completed; parallelization is not permission to group cards into broad implementation buckets.
- Shared engine primitives, shared templates, matrix schema, validators, public frontend contracts, and common test fixtures are merge-gated shared surfaces. Coordinate changes to these surfaces before shard-local card completion.
- If a card requires a shared engine or template change, implement the shared change first, run affected template/regression tests, and revalidate any completed cards with impacted interaction tags.
- Use a tiered test strategy to avoid 1704 full-suite runs: targeted per-card checks, targeted template/regression checks, shard-local validation, then full repository validation at shared-surface, shard-merge, and final gates.
- For an individual Card Task, run the narrowest reliable tests and validators that cover the card, its template family, its changed code paths, and its matrix row.
- Do not run the full repository test/build suite after every simple or vanilla card unless the suite is demonstrably fast and Codex records that decision.
- Run the full relevant suite immediately after shared engine changes, shared template changes, matrix/validator changes, frontend-contract changes, high-risk/ruling-sensitive regressions, shard merges, and final verification.
- Each shard must update matrix rows, scripts/templates, and tests for its assigned cards, then run local validators before merge.
- Use a tiered validation cadence: run targeted card/template tests for individual Card Tasks, shard-local validators before shard merge, and full repository gates only at shared-surface changes, shard merges, major milestones, and final verification.
- Do not run the full typecheck, full unit test suite, and full build after every individual Card Task unless that card changes shared engine behavior or a shared template.
- After every shard merge, run global matrix and Markdown backlog validators to prove no missing, duplicate, or conflicting card coverage.
- Use a tiered test cadence to avoid turning 1704 card tasks into 1704 full CI runs.
- For individual card tasks, run cheap card-local validation: matrix row validation, card-script/template registration checks, targeted unit tests, and affected template tests.
- Do not run full repository typecheck, full unit test suite, or full build after every individual card unless the card changes shared engine behavior, shared templates, validators, public contracts, or a high/ruling-sensitive interaction surface.
- For each parallel shard, run shard-local coverage checks, affected template tests, impacted interaction-tag tests, and typecheck before merge.
- After shared-surface changes and after shard merges, run global matrix/backlog validators and the smallest regression set covering the impacted interaction tags.
- Run full repository typecheck, full unit tests, contract tests, and build at milestone gates and final verification, not as the default after every card.
- Do not skip tasks.
- Do not skip cards.
- Do not mark a task complete unless its acceptance criteria pass.
- Preserve existing frontend contracts.
- Inspect the repository before assuming architecture.
- Use the repo’s actual language, framework, folder structure, and test tooling.
- Use `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` as the card source of truth.
- Do not rely on runtime natural-language parsing of card text.
- Every card must be explicitly represented in the implementation matrix.
- Every card must have an explicit card task in this task file.
- Templates may be used for repeated behavior, but every card still requires its own task.
- For each card, inspect the exact card text and determine whether existing engine logic is sufficient.
- For each card, consider whether implementing that card requires modifying previously implemented rules, templates, or card logic.
- For each card, add or update tests.
- For each card, update the card implementation matrix.
- Forbidden cards must be deck-blocked but still explicitly covered if they are part of the GOAT-era card pool.
- Non-GOAT cards must be deck-blocked and marked `notInGoatPool`.
- Stop only if progress is impossible without user input.
- Initial Route, Initial Template Family, Risk Level, and Interaction Tags in this file are preliminary routing hints inferred from `cards.json`; Codex must verify them against exact card text and GOAT rules before finalizing the matrix row.

### Test Execution Cadence and Performance Rules

The task queue must optimize for accuracy without forcing wasteful full-suite execution after every card.

- Individual Card Tasks require targeted validation: card-specific tests, exact template tests, affected interaction-tag tests, matrix row checks, and shard-local coverage checks.
- Full repository validation is required after foundation completion, any shared engine/template/validator/frontend-contract change, each shard merge, each major coverage milestone, and final verification.
- A vanilla or simple template card does not require a unique full-duel test if the shared template has strong tests and the card's matrix row proves exact attachment to that template.
- A custom, high-risk, or ruling-sensitive card requires targeted behavior tests, including timing, priority, Damage Step, targeting, public/private information, or interaction tests as applicable.
- A shard may batch local validation across a small group of low-risk template cards, but it must still update and validate every individual matrix row and Card Task.
- Shared-surface changes must be validated globally before additional shards depend on them.
- Skipped tests are allowed only when the repository lacks that test category or the shard records a concrete blocker; final verification must still pass all available gates.

### Required Implementation Statuses

Every card must be assigned exactly one final implementation status:

- `goatVanilla`
- `goatTemplate`
- `goatCustom`
- `goatForbiddenButScripted`
- `goatUnsupported`
- `notInGoatPool`

Temporary `goatUnsupported` is allowed during execution, but final validation must fail unless:

```text
goatUnsupported = 0
```

## Backend Foundation Tasks

### Foundation Task F-001: Repository inspection and architecture discovery

**Codex Task:**
Inspect the repository tree, package manager, backend source roots, existing game-engine files, public asset paths, tests, build configuration, and deployment assumptions.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Architecture notes identify the actual backend/game-engine entry points.
- Actual typecheck, test, and build commands are recorded.
- No backend implementation path is chosen before repository inspection.

### Foundation Task F-002: Frontend/backend contract audit

**Codex Task:**
Audit all API, socket, store, reducer, schema, and serialization contracts used by the existing frontend.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Existing frontend contracts are documented before backend changes.
- Backend changes preserve request/response/event names, payload shapes, IDs, and visibility guarantees unless the frontend is explicitly updated.
- Contract tests or fixtures cover the preserved public interface.

### Foundation Task F-003: Existing game-logic audit

**Codex Task:**
Inventory existing duel, turn, phase, chain, card, deck, player, zone, and action logic.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Existing reusable primitives are identified.
- Missing or incorrect primitives are listed before card work begins.
- No duplicate parallel engine is introduced unless the existing architecture requires replacement.

### Foundation Task F-004: Card data schema audit

**Codex Task:**
Inspect `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` and define the canonical card key, text reference, card-type mapping, legality mapping, and source-index convention.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The matrix extractor can load every source row.
- Source Index is treated as the zero-based array offset unless the repo already documents another convention.
- Passcode/id handling preserves leading zeros and string identity.

### Foundation Task F-005: GOAT rules ingestion

**Codex Task:**
Create or update engine rule notes for GOAT turn structure, spell speeds, priority, chains, ignition priority, summon response windows, Damage Step limitations, battle flow, and public/private information.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Rules notes cite the source material used by Codex.
- Engine tests cover priority, chain, turn, battle, and Damage Step basics before card-specific work.
- Card tasks can reference these shared rules instead of reimplementing them ad hoc.

### Foundation Task F-006: GOAT card-pool validation

**Codex Task:**
Implement a validator that compares every `cards.json` row against GOAT-pool status from the card data and any repo reference data.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every card receives a GOAT-pool status.
- Unknown GOAT status is not allowed in final mode.
- Non-GOAT cards, if any appear later, are deck-blocked in GOAT mode and marked `notInGoatPool`.

### Foundation Task F-007: GOAT banlist validation

**Codex Task:**
Implement banlist enforcement using `legality.restriction` and `legality.max_copies` from `cards.json` unless the repo has a stricter canonical GOAT banlist source.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Forbidden cards cannot be included in legal GOAT decks.
- Limited and semi-limited copy limits are enforced.
- Forbidden GOAT-pool cards remain represented in the matrix and behavior coverage.

### Foundation Task F-008: Core game-state model

**Codex Task:**
Implement or repair canonical duel state for players, life points, turn player, priority holder, phases, zones, card instances, face-up/face-down state, positions, controllers, owners, chain state, pending triggers, and random events.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- State transitions are deterministic and serializable.
- Owner/controller/location/visibility are tracked separately.
- Full duel reset and match reset restore clean state.

### Foundation Task F-009: Zone movement system

**Codex Task:**
Implement one authoritative zone-movement pipeline for Deck, Hand, Monster Zone, Spell/Trap Zone, Field Zone, Fusion Deck, GY, banished/remove-from-play, and temporary reveal locations.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every movement records cause, source card, previous zone, new zone, owner, controller, visibility, and timing metadata.
- Replacement effects can intercept legal movement points.
- Movement tests cover face-down cards, simultaneous movement, and public/private visibility.

### Foundation Task F-010: Turn and phase engine

**Codex Task:**
Implement the GOAT turn sequence, phase transitions, legal action windows, start/end hooks, and phase-specific restrictions.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Draw Phase, Standby Phase, Main Phase 1, Battle Phase, Main Phase 2, and End Phase are represented.
- Phase gates prevent illegal actions.
- Phase hooks are available for Standby and End Phase card effects.

### Foundation Task F-011: Priority and timing-window engine

**Codex Task:**
Implement priority handoff, open game state handling, summon response windows, ignition priority, trigger collection, and legal response prompts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The turn player receives correct GOAT priority windows.
- Summon response and post-resolution windows are tested.
- Illegal activations outside their timing windows are rejected.

### Foundation Task F-012: Chain engine

**Codex Task:**
Implement chain construction, spell speed rules, activation records, chain-link ordering, response legality, resolution order, and fizzled/invalid target handling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Chains resolve last-in-first-out.
- Spell Speed 1, 2, and 3 restrictions are enforced.
- Chain-link tests include negation, invalid targets, and simultaneous trigger setup.

### Foundation Task F-013: Targeting system

**Codex Task:**
Implement target declaration, target validation at activation, target revalidation at resolution, multi-target handling, and non-targeting effect handling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Activation fails if required legal targets are unavailable.
- Resolution handles missing or illegal targets according to GOAT rules.
- Tests distinguish targeting from non-targeting effects.

### Foundation Task F-014: Cost system

**Codex Task:**
Implement costs as paid before activation, with rollback prevention, cost legality checks, and support for discard, tribute, LP payment, banish/remove-from-play, send-to-GY, reveal, and return costs.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Costs cannot be paid if payment is illegal or impossible.
- Paid costs remain paid if activation is negated unless rules say otherwise.
- Tests cover discard, tribute, LP, reveal, and banish costs.

### Foundation Task F-015: Activation legality system

**Codex Task:**
Implement a shared legality checker for card activation, effect activation, timing, zones, controller, face-up/face-down state, costs, targets, chain restrictions, and Damage Step restrictions.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Illegal actions are rejected before state mutation.
- Legality errors are machine-readable for frontend display.
- Activation tests cover each major card and effect type.

### Foundation Task F-016: Continuous effect system

**Codex Task:**
Implement continuous effects, stat modifiers, level modifiers, type/attribute modifiers, name changes, attack restrictions, activation restrictions, and dependency-sensitive recalculation.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Continuous effects apply only while their source is active unless rules say otherwise.
- Stat recalculation is deterministic after every relevant state change.
- Tests cover overlapping modifiers and source removal.

### Foundation Task F-017: Replacement and prevention effect system

**Codex Task:**
Implement replacement and prevention hooks for destruction, battle destruction, damage, sending to GY, banish/remove-from-play, draw, discard, and attack prevention.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Replacement opportunities are offered at correct timing points.
- Prevention does not create illegal hidden state changes.
- Tests cover competing replacements and prevention expiration.

### Foundation Task F-018: Trigger effect system

**Codex Task:**
Implement mandatory and optional triggers, missed timing, simultaneous trigger ordering, trigger source memory, and trigger activation legality.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Mandatory triggers cannot be skipped.
- Optional `when...you can` effects can miss timing.
- Tests cover simultaneous triggers and source leaving field ambiguity.

### Foundation Task F-019: Ignition effect system

**Codex Task:**
Implement Spell Speed 1 ignition effects, main-phase activation windows, once-per-turn tracking, priority interaction, costs, and target selection.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Ignition effects cannot be activated in illegal phases or closed game states.
- GOAT ignition priority is tested.
- Once-per-turn usage persists correctly through zone changes when required.

### Foundation Task F-020: Quick effect system

**Codex Task:**
Implement Spell Speed 2 monster effects, response windows, chain insertion, Damage Step legality, costs, and negation interaction.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Quick effects can respond only when their text and timing allow.
- Damage Step quick-effect restrictions are enforced.
- Tests include trap-negation monster effects and activation-response effects.

### Foundation Task F-021: Flip effect system

**Codex Task:**
Implement flip summons, battle flips, effect-driven flips, FLIP trigger timing, face-down information handling, and post-flip position handling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Flip effects trigger when legally flipped face-up.
- Face-down identity remains private until revealed by rules.
- Tests cover flip summon, attacked face-down monster, and effect flip.

### Foundation Task F-022: Normal summon and set system

**Codex Task:**
Implement normal summon, normal set, once-per-turn normal summon usage, tribute requirements, summon response windows, and summon negation hooks.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Each player gets the correct normal summon/set allowance.
- Summon response windows open correctly.
- Summon/set tests preserve frontend action contracts.

### Foundation Task F-023: Tribute summon system

**Codex Task:**
Implement Level 5+ tribute requirements, tribute selection, tribute costs, set by tribute, summon-response handling, and restrictions from cards/effects.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Tribute counts are enforced.
- Tributed cards move through the canonical movement pipeline.
- Tests cover tribute summon, tribute set, and restricted summons.

### Foundation Task F-024: Special summon system

**Codex Task:**
Implement special summon procedures, effect special summons, inherent summons, summon limitations, face-up/face-down possibilities, and response windows.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Special summons validate zones, restrictions, and summon method.
- Summon response timing is correct.
- Tests cover hand, Deck, GY, banish, Fusion Deck, and token special summons where applicable.

### Foundation Task F-025: Fusion Deck and Fusion Summon system

**Codex Task:**
Implement Fusion Deck representation, fusion material validation, fusion spell/effect hooks, Metamorphosis-style level matching, Magical Scientist-style restrictions, and no-effect Fusion support.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Fusion monsters are not treated as Main Deck cards.
- Fusion materials and special Fusion procedures use canonical movement.
- Tests cover normal Fusion Summon, special Fusion Deck summons, and Fusion return/removal restrictions.

### Foundation Task F-026: Ritual Summon system

**Codex Task:**
Implement Ritual Spell activation, Ritual Monster validation, tribute level accounting, hand/field tribute sources, summon response windows, and Ritual-specific restrictions.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Ritual Monsters and Ritual Spells are linked by exact requirements.
- Tribute level and source restrictions are enforced.
- Tests cover successful and illegal Ritual Summons.

### Foundation Task F-027: Battle system

**Codex Task:**
Implement battle phase flow, attack declaration, attack target validation, replay, direct attacks, battle position restrictions, battle result processing, and battle-trigger timing.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Attack declaration and replay behavior are deterministic.
- Battle traps can respond in correct windows.
- Tests cover direct attacks, monster attacks, replays, and attack prevention.

### Foundation Task F-028: Damage Step system

**Codex Task:**
Implement GOAT Damage Step substeps, allowed activations, flip timing, damage calculation entry, damage calculation exit, and post-damage trigger windows.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Damage Step activation restrictions are enforced.
- Flip effects from battle are queued correctly.
- Tests include Book of Moon-like, stat modifier, battle trap, and damage trigger interactions.

### Foundation Task F-029: Damage calculation system

**Codex Task:**
Implement ATK/DEF comparison, battle damage, piercing, battle destruction marking, zero-ATK edge cases, modifiers during damage calculation, and simultaneous battle destruction.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Damage calculation uses current recalculated stats.
- Battle destruction and damage are recorded for later triggers.
- Tests cover attack vs attack, attack vs defense, piercing, ties, and modifiers.

### Foundation Task F-030: Equip system

**Codex Task:**
Implement equip activation, equip target legality, equip attachment, unequip/destruction when illegal, controller/owner distinctions, equip stat modifiers, and equip-trigger behavior.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Equip cards track their equipped card explicitly.
- Illegal equip state is cleaned up through canonical movement.
- Tests cover source removal, target removal, control changes, and re-equipping restrictions.

### Foundation Task F-031: Control-change system

**Codex Task:**
Implement temporary and permanent control changes, zone capacity handling, owner/controller separation, end-phase returns, equip interaction, attack restrictions, and reset behavior.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Control changes never alter ownership.
- End-phase control returns are scheduled and resolved correctly.

### Foundation Task F-032: Token system

**Codex Task:**
Implement token creation, ownership/controller, stats, type, attribute, level, position, tribute/battle eligibility, zone limits, and token disappearance on leaving field.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

### Foundation Task F-033: Counter system

**Codex Task:**
Implement counters on cards, counter placement/removal, counter-based costs, counter-based stat/effect changes, and serialization.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

### Foundation Task F-034: Once-per-turn, once-per-duel, and lingering-state system

Implement turn-scoped, duel-scoped, card-instance-scoped, and effect-scoped usage tracking, plus lingering restrictions and delayed effects.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Codex Task:**
Implement LP zero, deck-out, Exodia, Last Turn-style special win conditions, simultaneous loss handling, match state, and draw outcomes.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Deck-out and LP zero are distinguishable.

## Coverage, Matrix, and Validation Tasks

Codex must create and maintain a machine-readable implementation matrix. The matrix must include every card from `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` and each row must include at least:

- source index from `cards.json`
- passcode/id
- card name
- card type
- exact card text reference
- GOAT-pool status
- banlist status
- implementation status
- template family, if applicable
- custom script path, if applicable
- ruling notes
- interaction tags
- test file path
- coverage status
- unsupported reason, if temporarily unsupported

The matrix validator must fail if:

- Any card from `cards.json` is missing.
- Any card from `cards.json` appears more than once.
- Any passcode/id appears twice unless the source data intentionally models printings and a canonical key is documented.
- Any GOAT-pool card has no implementation status.
- Any legal GOAT-pool card is `goatUnsupported` in final mode.
- Any forbidden GOAT-pool card is deck-legal.
- Any forbidden GOAT-pool card is not scripted or explicitly covered.
- Any script references an unknown card.
- Any template references an unknown card.
- Any implemented card lacks tests.
- Any card task in this Markdown file is missing from the matrix.
- Any matrix row lacks a corresponding card task.
- Final mode has `goatUnsupported > 0`.

### Coverage Task M-001: Matrix source extractor

**Codex Task:**
Create a machine-readable implementation matrix generated from `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` source rows.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every row from `cards.json` appears exactly once in the matrix.
- Rows include source index, passcode/id, card name, card type, exact card text reference, GOAT-pool status, banlist status, implementation status, template family, custom script path, ruling notes, interaction tags, test file path, coverage status, and unsupported reason.
- The extractor preserves source order and leading-zero passcodes.

### Coverage Task M-002: Canonical card identity and duplicate validator

**Codex Task:**
Implement canonical identity validation for passcode/id plus documented handling for any intentional duplicate printings.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Any missing card identity fails validation.
- Any duplicate passcode/id fails unless a documented canonical-key exception exists.
- Any script or template reference to an unknown card fails validation.

### Coverage Task M-003: Implementation-status validator

**Codex Task:**
Enforce exactly one final implementation status per card row.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Allowed statuses are `goatVanilla`, `goatTemplate`, `goatCustom`, `goatForbiddenButScripted`, `goatUnsupported`, and `notInGoatPool`.
- Any GOAT-pool card without a status fails validation.
- Final mode fails if any legal GOAT-pool card is `goatUnsupported`.

### Coverage Task M-004: GOAT legality and deck-construction validator

**Codex Task:**
Validate deck legality against GOAT pool and restriction status.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Forbidden GOAT-pool cards are deck-blocked.
- Limited and semi-limited copy limits are enforced.
- Non-GOAT cards are deck-blocked in GOAT mode and marked `notInGoatPool`.

### Coverage Task M-005: Template and custom-script coverage validator

**Codex Task:**
Validate that every template and custom script is attached only to known card identities and has tests.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every implemented template has at least one test file path.
- Every custom card has targeted behavior tests.
- Every ruling-sensitive card has targeted behavior tests.

### Coverage Task M-006: Markdown backlog cross-validator

**Codex Task:**
Create a validator that parses `list_of_task.md` and cross-checks Card Task headings against the implementation matrix.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Any card task missing from the matrix fails validation.
- Any matrix row lacking a corresponding Card Task fails validation.
- Any card from `cards.json` that appears zero or multiple times in Card Task headings fails validation.

### Coverage Task M-007: Unsupported-card gate

**Codex Task:**
Implement development and final validation modes for `goatUnsupported`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Temporary `goatUnsupported` is allowed only during active execution with an unsupported reason.
- Final mode fails unless the coverage report shows `goatUnsupported = 0`.
- Unsupported reasons are machine-readable and actionable.

### Coverage Task M-008: Coverage report command

**Codex Task:**
Add or update a repo command that prints card coverage counts by status, route, template family, risk, and GOAT legality.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The report includes total source cards and total Card Task headings.
- The report prints `goatUnsupported = 0` only when final coverage is complete.
- The command is included in final verification docs.

### Coverage Task M-009: Parallel workstream sharding and merge protocol

**Codex Task:**
Define a parallel execution protocol for card implementation after foundation tasks, matrix extraction, validators, and shared engine primitives are in place. Create shard ownership rules that allow multiple Codex workers or branches to implement disjoint Card Task ranges without losing one-card-one-task traceability.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A workstream plan exists before parallel card implementation begins.
- Each shard has an explicit, non-overlapping ownership list using Card Task IDs, source-index ranges, or canonical card identities.
- No card identity is assigned to more than one active shard.
- Shared engine, shared template, validator, matrix-schema, and frontend-contract changes are treated as merge-gated shared-surface changes, not silent shard-local changes.
- Each shard can run a local coverage check for its assigned Card Tasks.
- Each shard defines its validation tier before implementation: targeted card/template tests, affected interaction tests, shard matrix validation, and post-merge global validation.
- Each shard does not run the full repository suite after every card by default; full gates run after shared-surface changes, shard merges, major milestones, and final verification.
- Each shard can produce a merge summary listing completed cards, matrix rows changed, scripts/templates changed, tests added or updated, validators run, and any intentionally deferred full-suite gates.
- Global validators fail if shard merges create duplicate card rows, missing card rows, missing Card Task coverage, duplicate Card Task coverage, stale unsupported reasons, or untested implemented behavior.
- The final merge validates all 1704 Card Tasks globally, not only per-shard.

### Coverage Task M-010: Tiered test execution strategy

**Codex Task:**
Define and enforce a test execution strategy that keeps the implementation accurate without requiring a full repository test/build run after every individual card. Classify tests into card-targeted tests, template-family tests, interaction/regression tests, shard-local validators, shared-surface gates, and final global gates.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Per-card completion requires targeted tests or exact template tests plus matrix validation for that card.
- Vanilla and stat-only cards may use base-rules/template tests plus matrix coverage rather than one bespoke full behavior test each.
- Template-backed cards may use shared template tests when the template exactly covers the card behavior, with targeted tests added for exceptions or card-specific timing/legality.
- Custom, high-risk, and ruling-sensitive cards require targeted behavior tests.
- Shard-local validation covers all cards assigned to the shard before merge.
- Full repository typecheck/test/build is required after shared engine changes, shared template changes, matrix/validator changes, frontend-contract changes, shard merges, and final verification.
- The strategy explicitly avoids 1704 full-suite runs unless the discovered repository test suite is fast enough and Codex records that this is cheaper than selective validation.

## Universal Per-Card Implementation Checklist

Codex must execute this checklist for every individual Card Task:

1. Locate the card in `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json`.
2. Confirm source index, canonical ID/passcode, name, type, and card text.
3. Confirm GOAT-pool status.
4. Confirm banlist status.
5. Read the exact card text.
6. Identify whether the card has no effect, template behavior, or custom behavior.
7. Identify all impacted systems: summon, set, flip, battle, Damage Step, damage calculation, targeting, cost, chain, priority, trigger timing, missed timing, continuous effect, replacement/prevention, equip, control change, token, counter, graveyard, banish/remove from play, deck search, deck shuffle, hand knowledge, public/private information, End Phase, Standby Phase, and win/loss.
8. Determine whether existing engine primitives are sufficient.
9. If existing logic is insufficient, modify the engine/template before implementing the card.
10. Implement the card as one of: vanilla/base rules, existing template, new template, custom script, forbidden-but-scripted, or not-in-GOAT deck-blocked.
11. Add or update targeted tests.
12. Add or update interaction tests when the card affects other card behavior.
13. Update the implementation matrix.
14. Run the appropriate validation tier: targeted card/template tests for the individual card, affected interaction-tag tests if relevant, matrix row validation, and shard-local coverage checks.
15. Run full repository gates only when this card changes shared engine logic, shared templates, validators, frontend contracts, or closes a shard/major milestone/final verification.
16. Do not mark the card task complete until its acceptance criteria pass under the appropriate validation tier.

## Cross-Card Interaction and Regression Tasks

### Regression Task R-001: Normal summon priority regression

**Codex Task:**
Verify turn-player priority and response windows after normal summon, normal set, tribute summon, and summon negation.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Targeted regression tests exist and pass.
- Failures update shared engine logic, templates, or individual card scripts instead of being bypassed.
- The implementation matrix and coverage report remain consistent after fixes.

### Regression Task R-002: Ignition priority regression

**Codex Task:**
Verify GOAT ignition priority in open game states, including priority after summon and after chain resolution.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Targeted regression tests exist and pass.
- Failures update shared engine logic, templates, or individual card scripts instead of being bypassed.
- The implementation matrix and coverage report remain consistent after fixes.

### Regression Task R-003: Chain response regression

**Codex Task:**
Verify legal and illegal responses by spell speed, timing, controller, face-up state, and Damage Step limitations.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Targeted regression tests exist and pass.
- Failures update shared engine logic, templates, or individual card scripts instead of being bypassed.
- The implementation matrix and coverage report remain consistent after fixes.

### Regression Task R-004: Chain resolution order regression

**Codex Task:**
Verify last-in-first-out resolution, negation, partial resolution, and no illegal state rollback.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Targeted regression tests exist and pass.
- Failures update shared engine logic, templates, or individual card scripts instead of being bypassed.
- The implementation matrix and coverage report remain consistent after fixes.

### Regression Task R-005: Target invalidation regression

**Codex Task:**
Verify effects with one target, multiple targets, and non-targeting effects when objects move, flip, or become illegal.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

## Final Verification Tasks

### Verification Task V-001: Run matrix/card-task consistency validation

**Codex Task:**
Run the Markdown backlog cross-validator and matrix validators in final mode.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every `cards.json` row appears exactly once in the matrix.
- Every `cards.json` row has exactly one explicit Card Task heading in `list_of_task.md`.
- No duplicate canonical card identity remains.

### Verification Task V-002: Run GOAT legality validation

**Codex Task:**
Run GOAT-pool, banlist, and deck-construction validation.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Forbidden cards are deck-blocked.
- Limited and semi-limited counts are enforced.
- Non-GOAT cards are deck-blocked in GOAT mode.

### Verification Task V-003: Run behavior coverage validation

**Codex Task:**
Run template, custom-card, ruling-sensitive, and interaction coverage tests.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every implemented template has tests.
- Every custom card has targeted tests.
- Every ruling-sensitive card has targeted tests.

### Verification Task V-004: Run frontend contract validation

**Codex Task:**
Run API/socket/state contract tests and any existing frontend integration checks.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Existing frontend contracts still pass.
- No private information is leaked through serialized state.
- Frontend-visible errors remain structured and stable.

### Verification Task V-005: Run repository commands

**Codex Task:**
Inspect available scripts and run the actual repository commands for typecheck, tests, and build. This is a full-suite milestone/final gate, not the default validation requirement for every individual card task.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- If npm scripts exist, prefer `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` when available.
- If the repo uses different commands, record and run those actual commands.
- Typecheck, unit tests, and build pass.
- The test cadence log shows card-local, template-family, interaction-tag, shard-local, shared-surface, milestone, and final validation were used at the appropriate scopes.

### Verification Task V-006: Validate parallel shard merge integrity

**Codex Task:**
Run global post-merge validation for every parallel shard or branch used during implementation. Confirm that shard-local completion did not create duplicate ownership, stale matrix rows, missing tests, inconsistent template mappings, or frontend contract drift.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every parallel shard has a merge summary.
- No Card Task is completed by more than one shard.
- No card identity appears in more than one final matrix row.
- Shared-surface changes have global tests, not only shard-local tests.
- Shard-local validation logs show targeted tests and affected interaction-tag regressions were run before merge.
- Global matrix, Markdown backlog, coverage, typecheck, unit test, contract test, and build gates pass after all shard merges.

## Final Task: Prove Complete GOAT Card Coverage

**Codex Task:**
Run all validation gates, coverage reports, typechecks, unit tests, integration tests, frontend contract tests, and build commands required by the repository. Prove that the full GOAT card implementation is complete for every row in `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Every card in `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` appears exactly once in the implementation matrix.
- Every card in `public/yugioh_cards/cards.json` has exactly one explicit card task in `list_of_task.md`.
- No duplicate passcodes or canonical IDs exist.
- No unknown GOAT-pool cards remain.
- No unsupported GOAT-pool legal cards remain.
- Forbidden cards are deck-blocked but still scripted or explicitly covered where applicable.
- Non-GOAT cards are deck-blocked in GOAT mode.
- Every implemented template has tests.
- Every custom card has targeted behavior tests.
- Every ruling-sensitive card has targeted behavior tests.
- Every card task has been marked complete only after its acceptance criteria passed.
- The tiered test cadence was followed: card-local checks for individual cards, template-family checks for template cards, targeted interaction regressions for impacted tags, shard-local checks before merge, and full repository gates at milestone/final verification.
- Tiered test execution records show targeted validation for per-card work and full repository validation at required shared-surface, shard-merge, and final gates.
- Parallel shard ownership, merge summaries, shared-surface changes, and global post-merge validators are complete if parallel workstreams were used.
- Coverage report shows:

```text
goatUnsupported = 0
```

- Existing frontend contracts still pass.
- Typecheck passes using the repository’s actual command.
- Unit tests pass using the repository’s actual command.
- Build passes using the repository’s actual command.

If the repository uses npm scripts, Codex should prefer these when available:

```bash
npm run typecheck

npm run build
```

Codex must inspect the repository and use the actual available commands.

## Codex Execution Goal

- Open `list_of_task.md`.
- Start with dependency-gated execution.
- Execute repository inspection, frontend/backend contract audit, foundation tasks, matrix tasks, validators, and the parallel workstream protocol before parallelizing card work.
- After those prerequisites pass, execute Card Tasks in explicit, non-overlapping parallel shards when available.
- Keep one-card-one-task traceability even when card work is parallelized.
- Do not skip foundation tasks.
- Do not skip card tasks.
- Do not skip cards that appear vanilla or simple.
- For each card task, inspect exact card text from `cards.json`.
- For each card task, decide whether engine/template/custom implementation is required.
- For each card task, update the matrix and tests.
- If a later card reveals a flaw in earlier engine/card logic, go back and fix the earlier logic.
- Keep frontend contracts intact.
- Run the appropriate validation tier after each relevant task: targeted tests for individual cards, shard-local validators before merge, global validators after shard merges, and full repository gates at shared-surface changes, major milestones, and final verification.
- Continue until the final coverage report shows `goatUnsupported = 0`.
- Stop only if progress is impossible without user input.
